rationale: Both miss the single most substantive ground-truth concern (aggregate MessageQueue overflow despite per-value SHM packing) and the #5793/video-transport discussion, so recall is low for both; X gets a small edge by echoing the ground-truth's manual-clamp/comment concern. X and Y independently converge on four of the same real issues (residual split-map race, swallowed SHM-unpack errors on the batch path, uncleared _completed_outputs, missing diagnostics on the sync wait path), which strongly corroborates precision for both, though X carries one incorrect technical claim (CancelledError/BaseException) in a nit. X pulls ahead on actionability with ready-to-apply code diffs for nearly every finding plus a unique, well-specified zero-element-view crash, whereas Y's findings are more description/evidence-heavy with fewer concrete patches and the output is cluttered with meta-report scaffolding and cuts off mid-sentence.
